items.title: Larry Gold interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 18, 2025
items.q: Look at Muhammad Ali. Muhammad Ali came out of that same school.

ctx.x: Indeed. It seems that technology and hip hop seem to go hand—in—hand with the production values. I wonder if you as a musician yourself was a bit surprised when melodic content became not necessary?

Yeah. But it was a slow ball. It wasn't like it was a fast ball. It started like in the early '80s. Late '70s already you had like the early rap songs coming out. So I knew, and then there were the DJs on the radio that all they all rhymed. Remember the old DJs? I mean the R&B DJs? They were all like poets and didn't know it. Look at Muhammad Ali. Muhammad Ali came out of that same school. Everything was a rhyme. Everything was a phrase that you could remember. So that didn't surprise me, especially being a…
Huh. What makes you keep going?
